prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single universal “best” roofing company for every Dallas roof replacement — the right contractor depends on your location, budget, roof type, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and the level of warranty/service you want. I can help you find the best fit. To start, tell me your ZIP code, whether this is an insurance job, and what roof material you want (asphalt shingles, metal, tile, etc.).

Meanwhile, here’s a practical way to find and vet top Dallas roofers:

How to find good candidates
- Search for local contractors with strong recent reviews on Google, Yelp, and Angi.
- Look for GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster or Owens Corning Platinum Preferred credentials — these indicate manufacturer training and warranty eligibility.
- Check BBB rating and complaint history.
- Ask neighbors or your HOA for recommendations if they’ve had recent roof work.

What to require/prove before hiring
- Proof of general liability insurance and workers’ compensation (ask to see certificates).
- A valid local business license and registration (Texas has no statewide roofing license, but cities may have requirements).
- A physical office address and a business phone number (not just a cell).
- References from recent customers with similar roofs.

Questions to ask each contractor
- Are you licensed/registered in the City of Dallas (if applicable) and will you obtain permits?
- Are you experienced with my roof type and slope?
- What products/brands do you use, and what warranties do they carry (manufacturer + workmanship)?
- Will you provide a written, itemized estimate and a fixed price?
- How long will the job take? What is your clean-up policy?
- How do you handle hidden damage or decking replacement?
- What is the payment schedule? (Avoid large up-front demands.)

What to compare in estimates
- Tear-off vs. re-cover (how many layers will be removed).
- Type and grade of shingles or materials.
- Underlayment, ventilation, drip edge, flashing, ice/water barrier details.
- Nail type and spacing, deck repairs included or priced separately.
- Manufacturer and contractor warranty terms and length.

Red flags
- High-pressure sales, storm-chasing crews without a local presence.
- No written estimate or reluctance to sign a contract.
- Requests for large cash payments up front.
- Very low bids that seem unrealistic.

If you want, tell me your ZIP code and any other details (insurance claim, roof size, material) and I’ll pull together a short list of well-reviewed Dallas roofers that fit your needs and include contact links and what to verify for each.
